feedback: Written before this candidate races. The evidence supports holding ±0.03 m with 16 mm footprints. Race 2 (entityR2B, 356.98) is the best result: oval finished 15 of 20 with max_error 0.048, but s-bend and slalom still lost the line at 1.15 and 1.10 events per run with max_error at the limit. Race 3 (entityR2B, 235.88) tested ±0.04 m, which cut oval finishes to 5 of 20 and left s-bend and slalom line loss at 1.0 and 1.15. So the wider spread did not fix the failure it was meant to fix, and the spread is not the limiter on those tracks. Your lead move is a reasonable single-variable test. Race 2 oval steering_oscillation was 0.31, above the 0.2 threshold we set for moving the sensors forward. I have kept the controller identical to race 2, so any change in the next race comes from y alone. Once the race reports, use this rule. If oval steering_oscillation falls and oval finishes hold near race 2 levels, keep y = 0.06. If oval finishes fall, return the lead to y = 0.05. If s-bend and slalom still lose the line at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06, hold the geometry and I will tune gains.
requested_changes: Keep ±0.03 m spread, 16 mm footprints and y = 0.06 for the next race, so the lead is the only geometry change against race 2.
If oval finishes fall below about 12 of 20 while oscillation improves, return y to 0.05, because the lead cost reach on the oval.

Optional, untested alternative if s-bend and slalom still lose the line at 1 or more with the spread held: try seven 16 mm sensors at ±0.03 m (about 10 mm pitch) to add coverage without widening. This has no race evidence yet and should be treated as exploration.
